title: I keep seeing those gorgeous games built with ai on webs with threejs or some sorts. Are they actually exportable to any proper game engine to actually ship?
author: Prior-Meeting1645

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: No need to use a game engine if it works well. You can always wrap them in something like electron if you want to provide a more offline feeling experience.

replies.author: Prior-Meeting1645
replies.body: Interesting thank you will have a look

comments.author: fued
comments.body: None of them are even close to being game ready, they are pretty prototypes tho

replies.author: Prior-Meeting1645
replies.body: Oh yes definitely. But they’re very low effort I was thinking with the right effort they can definitely be made into something pretty well polished. Lots of them look better than what I did with lots of work with the claude blender mcp. But then again there’s so many fake videos that are using pre made assets or what not its hard to know these days lol. But I think it’s a fact that they have better training data in threejs rather than in making blender scripts

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
Three.js is a JavaScript library for the browser for 3D graphics. 

If you want something built in a game engine them you need to build it in that engine. You can't just convert a game automatically between engines.

replies.author: Prior-Meeting1645
replies.body: I have been experimenting with asking the ai to generate it in threejs then exporting it as glbs to an engine like godot. What do you think of this approach? It was even able to preserve some of the animations

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: You can do that but it will probably only work with basic animations, you will also then have to manually add gdscript for any interaction.
